This PDF is the curriculum vitae of **Timothy J. Gates, Ph.D., P.E.**, a senior faculty member in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at **Michigan State University (MSU)**.  Gates has been with MSU since 2015, progressing from Associate Professor (2007‑2013) to Professor (2021‑present) and serving as Associate Chair for Undergraduate Studies since 2020.  His earlier academic appointments include four years as Associate/Assistant Transportation Researcher at the **Texas Transportation Institute (TTI)** (2000‑2003), a six‑year stint as Assistant Professor and then Associate Professor at **Wayne State University (WSU)** (2007‑2015), and a doctoral and master’s degree from MSU (BS 1999, MS 2000, PhD 2007).  He holds an MS in Civil Engineering (Transportation) from MSU and a PhD in Civil Engineering (Transportation) from the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

Gates’s professional society membership lists the Institute of Transportation Engineers (Michigan section, 2007‑present), and he is a licensed Professional Engineer in Michigan (no. 6201062278, granted 2015).  His honors include the Withrow Exceptional Service Award (MSU, 2024), multiple “Best Paper” recognitions from the Transportation Research Board (TRB) Traffic Control Devices Committee and Operational Effects of Geometrics Committee (2020–2022), the William Bradley Outstanding Faculty Member Award (MSU ASCE Chapter, 2017), and a high‑value research award from the AASHTO Research Advisory Committee (2013).  In addition, he has served on the FHWA Dwight D. Eisenhower Graduate Fellowship program (2003‑2005; 1999‑2000) and was a 2004 graduate fellow.

The CV lists an extensive **research record**.  Notable recent grant projects (2024–2027) include evaluations of digital speed limit signs in work zones (MDOT), rest‑area prioritization, and new countermeasures for adverse driving behavior.  Earlier awards include the FHWA Dwight D. Eisenhower Graduate Fellowship (2004) and the Texas Transportation Institute New Researcher Award (2002).

The **publications** section enumerates over three hundred refereed journal articles (beginning in 2006) and numerous conference proceedings.  The earliest cited paper is “The Safety and Cost‑Effectiveness of Approach Guardrail for Bridges on Low Volume Roads” (TRB, 2006), followed by subsequent works on speed limits, traffic control devices, crash‑reduction interventions, and dynamic speed feedback signs.  Gates’s most recent 2025 works include a road‑traffic analysis on a freeway corridor with hard‑shoulder running and a study of driver response to bridge‑deck warning systems.  He also authors review articles such as “A Comprehensive Review of Dynamic Speed Feedback Signs” (Traffic & Transportation, 2024).  His co‑authorships involve recurring collaborators such as P.T. Savolainen, Kakan Dey, Peter Savolainen, and J. Kay.

The CV also documents his **teaching** load: course titles (e.g., CE 341 Transportation Engineering, CE 449 Highway Design, CE 843/891 Advanced Highway Design and Traffic Control), enrollment numbers, and average SIRS ratings, demonstrating robust undergraduate and graduate instruction.  He is also the faculty advisor for several doctoral and master’s theses, including work by Jonathan Kay, Anthony Ingle, and others.

On the **service** side, Gates currently chairs the MSU College‑wide Undergraduate Curriculum Committee and serves as a key member of the TRB Standing Committee on Road User Measurement and Evaluation (ACH50) and the Traffic Control Devices Committee (AHB50/ACP55).  He has an active role as handling editor for the TRB’s Transportation Research Record since 2019 and coordinates reviewer activities for several transportation journals.  Added professional duties include providing testimony to the Michigan State Senate transportation committee on raising speed limits and organi­zing several professional translation series and field demonstrations.

In sum, the document presents a detailed portrait of Gates’s academic career trajectory, scholarship output, teaching responsibilities, grant activities, awards, and professional service.  The CV is up‑to‑date through January 31, 2025 and highlights his major contributions to traffic safety research, especially around dynamic speed feedback, work‑zone safety, and highway geometry.
